fact_check.the_95_88_195_87_claim: MISLEADING. The GTA+ trial is one FREE month, so after launch only 11 months are paid inside the first 12 months. 'One year costs $95.88' is true only as 12 paid months, which are months 2-13, i.e. 'a year AFTER the free month'. 'His real total for the year is $195.87' is FALSE as worded. Re-computed: 11 x 7.99 = $87.89, so the true first-12-month total is $99.99 + $87.89 = $187.88. $195.87 is the 13-month total. 'More than double' still holds either way ($79.99 x 2 = $159.98). The script's own math_check admits this nuance, yet ships 'for the year'. The research file's 'year one' label is itself wrong and should not be inherited.
beyond_sources: Lines 3-4 'There is no disc / It is just a download code' are stated as flat fact; the cited tech-insider source is 'as reported' (the research marks it that way). Needs 'reportedly' or similar, or a primary source.

$7.99/month rests on a 2024 TweakTown article; no 2026 primary source confirms the price GTA+ converts to when the GTA VI trial ends. The IBTimes source only says the trial can convert to paid. Prefer 'at the usual seven ninety-nine' or verify on a store page.

Hook 'does NOT cost $79.99. It costs way more.' overstates the sources: the Standard price IS $79.99. The extra $20 upgrade and the GTA+ charge are Benny's optional or forgotten choices, not mandatory costs. Calling it the 'real total' implies everyone pays it.

Line 1-2 'preorder' plus 'It is launch day' conflict: you cannot preorder on release day. Use 'launch day purchase' or drop 'preorder' from the spoken hook while keeping the 'digital preorder' trial claim consistent (source says digital pre-orders get the trial).
Launch date is sourced to Rockstar's page and used only as 'launch day': OK.
